chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Going to London: Latimore and the Charveau engagement
summary: The orchestra changed repertoire every three weeks; Latimore, as business manager, financed and booked the London engagement through Henri Charveau.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, how did it happen that the orchestra went to London then?
I think we changed the repertory every three weeks.
Well, then, it was the same group more or less that had been in the States?

Oh, yes. I mean we probably had one or two replacements that didn't want to come over. We had -- one of the replacements was the name I showed you on there, Sainave. He was a student at the French Conservatory in Paris.
But we knew, Mr. Latimore knew that our flute player, Mr. Adams, who was with me at the Submarine Boat Corporation -- did you read about that?
Well, he decided not to leave America.

Well, we were engaged by Mr. Henri Charveau through Mr. Lattimore. Mr. Lattimore was a businessman, and right after World War I, there were plenty opportunities for artists abroad, you see. And Mr. Lattimore, being a very intelligent person, and a very, very good businessman, he grasped the opportunity and probably proposed the orchestra, 'cause he was more a business manager and everything. He footed all the expenses, you see.
He was a manager, running like a booking office, like. And he got us this engagement. It was a very, very good engagement for us.
